audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Lucian/Skill/Skill/Lucian — it gave Lucian the 2+ items stage and called Levels 1-3 even, exactly inverting this page's own prose ('Levels 1-3 are yours', 'This is Trundle's game, not yours' late).
audit.why: The packet chart (Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Skill, Skill, Trundle) matches every why line: Trundle is a dashless melee with no range at 1-3, the lane evens from 4 as Frozen Domain lets him stick, and drain-tank items plus Subjugate reclaim the late game.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Lucian / Lucian / Lucian / Skill / Skill / Skill / Trundle in both layers, ratings adjusted, and the label moved off 'Favoured' onto EVEN to match a 47.21% win rate.

audit.why: Four spikes present in order: Lvl 2-3 Lucian window, Lvl 6 Subjugate, 1st item Trundle sustain, 2+ items drain-tank. One typo inside spikes[2] ('Bramback') fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown' appears nowhere in either layer, while the page's central instruction — repeated in tradeBad, dontsFull[1], report[9] and breakdown.cooldowns — is to fight only when that dash is available.
audit.why: It is in Riot's own text for Lucian's E. A player counting a flat 16 seconds is playing with worse information than the game gives him: the dash returns early exactly in the trades where his double-shots landed, and stays gone in the trades where they missed. The mirror flagged this as the single biggest addition on the matchup and it applies identically from this side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp's auto-reset and Frozen Domain's effect on the trade are both absent from the full layer, and Subjugate is described as if it were a lockdown ('never take a long duel into it').
audit.why: Q: 'Trundle bites his opponent, dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage' on a flat 3.5s, 300 range, with the autoReset flag — so the tell is the wind-up animation, not a cast bar, which is the flagged autoreset-burst-tell interaction. W: 'gaining Attack Speed, Move Speed, and increased healing from all sources while on it' — the attack speed advantage in this lane is his zone, on his patch of ground, so you fight off it. R: 'immediately steals a percent of his target's Health, Armor and Magic Resistance... doubled over 4 seconds' — a stat theft with no CC at all, 650 range, 120/100/80s. The mirror states the same three from his side.
audit.corrected: All three written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[3].why and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' — confirmed, not one number on the page.
audit.why: Chomp 3.5s flat, Pillar of Ice 21/19.5/18/16.5/15s at 1000 range, Frozen Domain 18s, Subjugate 120/100/80s. Pillar is the one that matters for a dash champion: it is real impassable terrain, so it can wall Relentless Pursuit outright.
audit.corrected: Concrete wait-for-X-then-Y line added to report[9].t; Pillar's terrain and cooldown to dosFull[2].d.

audit.why: report[8].t already carries 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', which covers King's Tribute healing him off every dying unit near him. No change needed.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Subjugate — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Subjugate steals armour, MR and HP and doubles it over 4s — execute with it, never open into it.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: Your first item still threatens, but King's Tribute heals him off every minion dying near him — anti-heal or nothing.

edits.before: You fall off relative to top-lane scalers — convert the lead into towers and roams before the 3-item brawlers arrive.
edits.after: Drain-tank items plus Subjugate's stat theft win any extended fight — kite for your team, never duel him.

edits.before: - Trundle Subjugate: matchup-defining — Steals your resists and HP — never take a long duel into it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Trundle Subjugate: 120/100/80s at 650 range — it steals HP, armour and MR and doubles over 4s. Chomp is a flat 3.5s auto-reset: his wind-up is the cue, not a cast bar. - Your E comes back faster every time a Lightslinger shot lands.

edits.before: Steals your resists and HP — never take a long duel into it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Chomp is a flat 3.5s auto-reset that saps your AD — his wind-up is the tell, not the cast bar.

edits.before: Trundle burns Subjugate on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice is real terrain — it walls your dash. 21s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Trundle’s Subjugate: Steals your resists and HP — never take a long duel into it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Relentless Pursuit is 16s, but every Lightslinger shot that lands refunds part of it — count your procs, not seconds.

edits.before: Commit on Subjugate’s cooldown, on your first item spike, and with your jungler’s setup. His answer goes first; yours goes last.
edits.after: Wait for Chomp's 3.5s to be spent, then step in; wait out Pillar of Ice's 21s, then commit. His answer goes first; yours last.
